messages:
Chris Nguyen: Thanks for the infra section earlier — starting a follow-up thread to capture Qs on GPU supply, region rollouts, and autoscaler plans. Please drop quick questions or callouts and well answer live.
Olivia Park: Quick clarifying Q: is APAC on-track or do we expect a phased delivery? Heard conflicting notes about networking first vs compute first.
Chris Nguyen: Short: phased. Compute (GPU nodes) prioritized, networking/interconnects next. APAC earliest compute availability: late Q3, but thats best-effort dependent on vendor shipments.
Anika Bose: If supply gets constrained, what are our prioritized mitigations for Hosted vs Dedicated?
Chris Nguyen: Hosted: model-variant routing, aggressive batching, and temporary cross-region routing for non-latency-critical customers. Dedicated: we honor pinned capacity per contracts; if were forced, we offer temporary burst alternatives or compensatory credits.
David Romero: For the legal team: confirm we have a list of customers who signed before the capacity lock date. I need to cross-check contract language and priority buckets.
Leo Zhang: Autoscaler detail: will new autoscaler use model-level signals (token_rate estimates) or only infra metrics? Curious about per-model batch targets.
Infra Bot: deploy-bot: autoscaler/v2 deploy to canary clusters started 2026-07-12T09:11Z 4 nodes targeted.
Mike Patel: Telemetry: when autoscaler changes batching, will Console show delta in estimated cost per-route? Finance needs that to approve spend.
Rachel Kim: How disruptive is a move to 4-bit quant for r5? Do we have a rollout plan that includes eval gating?
Priya Singh: For rollouts: prefer per-region canaries. We should avoid global flips. Is that supported out-of-the-box?
Samira Ortiz: Question for infra-sre: how do we ensure SLOs during cross-region fallback? Some customers are latency-sensitive and will need clear opt-in docs.
Chris Nguyen: Answers quick: autoscaler v2 will ingest model hints (estimated_tokens_per_sec) plus GPU util. Initial rollout uses heuristic weights; later we'll tune with live telemetry.
Chris Nguyen: Console: yes, next Console release includes a batching impact panel where you can compare estimated CPU/GPU cost per 1k tokens before/after batching.
Chris Nguyen: Quantization: research shows 4-bit can reduce memory ~40% and improve throughput ~20-30% on supported kernels; but quality varies. We will gate by eval suites per-model and include a per-route opt-in.
Chris Nguyen: Canary per-region: supported. Well flip region flags so we can iterate US -> EMEA -> APAC. Auto-rollback will trigger on regression thresholds.
Olivia Park: If APAC slips, can we route traffic to US-West for a transitional period? Need to draft customer-facing note about expected latency implications.
Chris Nguyen: Yes, cross-region fallback is possible as an opt-in policy. Default is opt-in; product needs to decide if we should offer opt-out fallback for specific SLAs.
David Romero: Ill compile the contract list and share with infra/legal. Please tag the priority bucket in the spreadsheet.
Anika Bose: Can someone paste a tiny example autoscaler policy snippet? Even pseudo-config helps engineering mock.
Chris Nguyen: Example (toy):
```
policies:
  - id: fast-burst
    trigger: model_hints.token_rate > 40000 or gpu_util > 0.8
    action:
      scale: add_nodes(2)
      prefer: same_region
      cooldown: 90s
  - id: quality-protect
    trigger: p99_latency > 600ms
    action: route_to: quantized_variant:false
```
Mike Patel: For visibility: will Console indicate which requests were served by quantized variants vs full-precision? We need that to correlate quality regressions.
Chris Nguyen: Yes 5 we will add per-request metadata tags for variant, quant level, and routing decision so Console/eval pipelines can filter.
Leo Zhang: Who owns the autoscaler SLO dashboard so we can add synthetic checks?
Chris Nguyen: Leo to own initial dashboard. Leo, please coordinate with DevEx for synthetic tests and alert thresholds.
Infra Bot: incident-bot: created INF-4820 "autoscaler canary monitoring: synthetic failing p99" assigned to Leo Zhang.
Priya Singh: Ops note: ops runbook will include steps to disable cross-region failover and apply customer-specific policies. Need owners for runbook review.
Samira Ortiz: Also add a checklist item for customer communication for Dedicated customers if we plan any temporary routing changes.
Rachel Kim: Eval gating: can we lock which evals will qualify a model for quant rollout? I want to ensure we measure hallucination and instruction-following.
Chris Nguyen: Yes, well publish the eval suite per-model. Research will own the eval gating with product sign-off.
Olivia Park: Timeline ask: when will the owners doc land? Teams need deadlines to plan.
Chris Nguyen: Ill publish a short timeline + owner matrix by EOD Friday. Also scheduling a follow-up sync next Tuesday 9am PT for rollout owners.
David Romero: Thanks  Ill circulate contracts to legal and infra.
Anika Bose: Thanks  will wait for the example policies and the owners doc to add tests.
Chris Nguyen: Appreciate the questions. Ill bump when the doc is live and link it here. Closing thread once doc posted.
